stories.title: Stan Wawrinka's Career Is Over — Lost to Lehečká in Basel

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Stan Wawrinka's career is over. Lehečká d. Wawrinka 7-5, 7-6(2) in Basel R1 — the final match of a career that produced 3 Grand Slam titles. Three-time Major winner. Forever a champion. #Tennis #Wawrinka

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Three Grand Slams. An epic rivalry with Djokovic. Comeback after comeback. Wawrinka played his last match Tuesday in Basel — in his home country — the way he played his whole career: on his own terms. #Tennis #StanTheMan

facebook.image_caption:
Stan Wawrinka — three-time Grand Slam champion — played his last ATP match Tuesday in Basel.

Seven years after his last Major title, and decades after picking up a racquet as a kid in Switzerland, the legend took his bow.

Some players win once. Stan won three times — and every single time, nobody saw it coming. That's what made it magic.

article.headline: Stan Wawrinka's Career Is Over After Basel First-Round Loss to Lehečká

stories.title: Djokovic Falls to Struff for First Time — Basel Campaign Over, ATP Finals Bid Fading

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: UPSET: Struff has beaten Djokovic in Basel — the FIRST TIME he has ever beaten Novak on the ATP Tour. Three sets. Djokovic's Basel campaign is over. His ATP Finals bid just got a lot harder. #Tennis #SwissIndoors

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Djokovic is out of Basel. He sits outside the top 8 in the Race to Turin. Paris Masters starts tomorrow. Likely his last chance to qualify for the ATP Finals. Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton have clinched. #Tennis #ATPFinals

facebook.image_caption:
Struff d. Djokovic. First career win for the German against Novak.

Basel is over for Djokovic — but his ATP Finals bid isn't finished yet. Paris starts tomorrow.

article.headline: Djokovic Falls to Struff for First Time in Basel — ATP Finals Bid Now Depends on Paris

stories.title: Zverev Clinches Year-End No. 1, Vienna Quarterfinals Set

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Alexander Zverev has clinched the year-end No. 1 ATP ranking. A win over Griekspoor in Vienna sealed it. He'll hold the top spot on November 2. Roland Garros finalist. US Open champion. No. 1. #Tennis #Zverev

facebook.image_caption:
Year-end No. 1.

Zverev clinched it Wednesday in Vienna. He'll be the ATP's top-ranked player to end 2026 — a year when the sport's top stars dealt with injury and absence.
